title: Benefits of a Medical Marijuana Card: What It Gets You
h1: Why Register as a Medical Cannabis Patient? The Benefits, Explained
metaDescription: Benefits of a medical marijuana card, from lower taxes and access at 18 to caregivers and legal protection, plus the trade-offs and how it works in Michigan.

body:
The benefits of a medical marijuana card depend on where you live, but they usually fall into a few buckets: legal protection, lower taxes, access before 21, caregivers who can help, and different limits on buying, carrying or growing. Even in Michigan, where adults 21 and older can shop recreationally, those differences make a card worthwhile for some people.

## Why people register where adult-use is legal

If anyone 21 and older can walk into a store, why register? For many patients the answer is practical: a card can lower what you pay, open the door at 18, let someone else shop or grow for you, and add legal protections. Whether that is worth the paperwork depends on your state, your age and how often you buy.

## Legal protections, and how they vary

Medical programs protect registered patients in ways that differ from state to state. In Michigan, a patient or caregiver is protected from arrest only when they can show police a valid registry card along with photo ID. An application or a physician’s form doesn’t count as a temporary card.

## Lower taxes

Medical purchases can be taxed less than recreational ones. In Michigan, adult-use purchases carry a 10% excise tax plus the 6% sales tax, while medical sales to registered patients skip the excise. On a $100 purchase, that’s about $16.60 in tax for adult use versus $6 with a card.

## Access by age, and caregivers

Adult-use shopping in Michigan starts at 21, but adults 18 and older can register as patients on their own. A minor can qualify with certifications from two physicians and a parent or legal guardian who serves as caregiver. Adult patients can name a caregiver too, someone at least 21 who passes a criminal background check, to shop or grow on their behalf.

## Possession, home grow and product guidance

Limits vary by state. In Michigan, a registered patient can have up to 2.5 ounces of usable marijuana on hand and, if no caregiver grows for them, up to 12 plants in an enclosed, locked space. Our [Michigan cannabis law guide](/cannabis-laws-by-state/michigan/) has the adult-use limits for comparison.

Certification also means a physician has evaluated you, which makes your doctor the right person to ask about products, doses and interactions with your medications. Budtenders can explain labels and formats, but they don’t write treatment plans.

## Trade-offs to weigh

- **Fees and renewals.** Michigan’s fee is $40, and a card lasts two years. You can renew starting 90 days before it expires.
- **Federal law.** As of October 2026, federal law places marijuana covered by a state medical license in Schedule III, while all other marijuana stays in Schedule I. The change doesn’t say patients may carry it across state lines or onto federal property, so consider both off-limits.
- **Firearms.** Federal law bars unlawful drug users from having guns. In June 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court held in *United States v. Hemani* that the government couldn’t apply that ban to a marijuana user prosecuted for his use alone, with no evidence he was dangerous. The ruling was narrow, so gun owners should talk to a lawyer before registering.
- **Travel.** Michigan honors valid cards from other states at stores licensed to sell medical cannabis, but every state sets its own policy.

## How the benefits of a medical marijuana card look in Michigan

Patients can start at 18, pay only the 6% sales tax and can name a caregiver, and they must be Michigan residents. Our guide to [Michigan medical card benefits](/blog/michigan-medical-marijuana-card-benefits/) goes deeper on whether a card pays off here.

To apply, you need a physician’s certification, proof of Michigan residency and the $40 fee. Patients without a caregiver can apply online through the Cannabis Regulatory Agency; naming a caregiver means using the paper packet. See [how to apply for a Michigan card](/getting-a-medical-card/) for every step.

High Society welcomes medical patients 18 and older with a valid card. Bring your card and a photo ID to any of our [Michigan stores](/dispensary-locations/), and our budtenders will help you compare products.

faq.q: Is a card worth it where recreational sales are legal?
faq.a: It can be, especially if you’re 18 to 20, buy often enough for the tax savings to add up, or need a caregiver. In Michigan, skipping the 10% excise tax saves about $10.60 in tax on every $100 you spend. Weigh that against the $40 fee every two years, the physician visit and federal issues such as firearms.

faq.q: Can a medical card affect gun ownership?
faq.a: It can, though the law shifted in 2026. Federal law bars unlawful drug users from having firearms, and in June 2026 the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that ban couldn’t be applied to a marijuana user based on his use alone. The ruling was narrow, so ask a lawyer if you own or plan to buy a gun.

faq.q: Does a medical card work in other states?
faq.a: Sometimes. Michigan honors valid cards from other states at stores licensed to sell medical cannabis, but each state sets its own policy, so check before you travel. Either way, don’t carry cannabis across state lines, which a state card doesn’t protect.
